rationale: The study applies the existing LiSep LSTM (developed on MIMIC-III) as-is to an external European cohort and additionally retrains it on pooled MIMIC-III+AUMC data, a supervised septic-shock prediction task; PFI is an explainability method and is not tagged. Domains centre on ICU-based clinical prediction of septic shock using EHR databases.

The paper trains multivariable logistic regression models on retrospective real-world hospitalization data to predict 15-day and 30-day readmission, a supervised prediction task in health services research. AUC, Brier score, calibration, and bootstrap/temporal validation are evaluation methods, not additional models.

Environmental radiation monitoring study (gamma dose rate, radiological hazard) best captured as Physics/Environmental science. Four supervised algorithms (SVM, linear regression, decision tree, random forest) were trained on the study's own data, with random forest performing best, so classical ML plus ensemble learning families apply.

The paper trains supervised ensemble tree regressors (random forest, gradient boosted regression trees, XGBoost) on its own halide-perovskite dataset to predict band gap energies, with feature importance analysis that is not itself a model type. The subject is materials/property prediction in physical chemistry, so Chemistry with Computational chemistry and Machine learning fits best; no tier-3 term matches materials band-gap modelling.

A pure computer-science/deep-learning paper introducing BDLO, a learnable operator replacing the shifting block in MLP-mixer vision architectures, with no biomedical subject matter. The BDLO-equipped CycleMLP, HireMLP and AS-MLP models are trained from scratch in a supervised manner on CIFAR/ImageNet classification benchmarks; Optuna and the Wilcoxon test serve only hyperparameter tuning and statistical testing, so they are not model types.

The paper trains PINNs on LiDAR data, embedding physical constraints (Ekman balance, shear power-law) in the loss, so models are trained in this study under supervised learning with physics-informed deep learning as the family. The subject is atmospheric boundary-layer wind profiling (physics/environmental science), with no biomedical domain terms applicable.

The paper trains its own deep learning model, Vib2Conf (with an attentional resampler and integrated Mixture-of-Experts), in a supervised manner on labelled spectrum-to-conformation benchmarks. The subject is discriminating 3D conformations of small molecules from vibrational spectra, fitting analytical/computational chemistry and structure prediction/modelling domains.

The study trains genomic, phenomic, and multiomics prediction models on its own wheat field-trial data to predict grain yield, a clearly supervised prediction setting. However, the abstract names no specific algorithm or architecture (only generic 'parametric and non-parametric models'), so model_type and model_family are left empty; domains reflect crop-breeding genomics with genotype-to-phenotype quantitative-genetic prediction.

A two-dimensional U-Net configured with nnU-Net v2 was trained from scratch on expert-annotated laparoscopic video frames for supervised multiclass/binary semantic segmentation of the IMA and IMV. The subject is a surgical clinical proof-of-concept using medical video imaging, so Medicine/Surgery/Imaging and Medical imaging apply.

The paper's subject is the chemistry of ZIF/MOF polymorph selection, studied via metadynamics molecular simulations and newly developed neural network classifiers, fitting Computational chemistry, Machine learning, and Molecular dynamics/modelling. The neural network classifiers are trained in-house on simulation-derived, polymorph-labelled structure databases (supervised learning), and since no deep architecture is specified, the plain neural network maps to classic neural network.

A multimodal schizophrenia study combining blood transcriptomics (gene co-expression modules, an unsupervised step) with resting-state fMRI to train a diagnostic classifier on the paper's own data. The abstract names no specific classification algorithm, and the co-expression module pipeline falls under excluded bioinformatics analyses, so model_type and model_family are empty.

The paper prompts common commercial LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) with design principles to generate de novo ligand-binding protein sequences, with no training or fine-tuning of any model in the study. Unnamed structure prediction is only used for filtering, so it is not tagged as a model type.

The study trains a Random Forest on its own untargeted UHPLC-HRMS metabolomics profiles to identify processing-stable phenolic markers (supervised), while hierarchical clustering of the same data is an unsupervised step used alongside it; SHAP is explainability and targeted quantification is not ML. The subject domain is plant metabolomics of small-molecule phenolics in edible Asteraceae species.

A pretrained CNN-based visual saliency/attention model is applied as-is to movie clips, with its filters decomposed and their temporal responses used as regressors in GLM analysis of fMRI data; nothing is trained in this study. The abstract names only the CNN (no clustering algorithm or other model is specified), and GLM/eye-tracking are excluded as statistical analyses.

The paper is a single-cell transcriptomic study of immune mechanisms in diabetic kidney disease, focusing on macrophage reprogramming and tubule-derived paracrine signaling, hence the immunology/nephrology and transcriptomics/regulation tags. Its computational tools (SCENIC, CellChat, NicheNet, pseudotime trajectory analysis) are bioinformatics network/pipeline analyses rather than named ML models, and no learning, fine-tuning, or prompting of an AI/ML model is described, so all modelling fields are empty.

The paper's subject is a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic inference tool, whose only ML component is a machine-learning-based branch support prediction model introduced as part of this release (hence trained in this study, supervised by nature of predicting a target). The abstract names no algorithm or model family for that predictor, so model_type and model_family are left empty.

All models are fit on the study's own data: an SVM classifier trained on Raman spectra and LASSO/Random Forest/XGBoost used for supervised feature selection on proteomics, so model_use is 'trained in this study' with a supervised paradigm. The domain is analytical biomedicine of breast cancer, integrating Raman spectroscopy with quantitative proteomics for diagnostics and drug-mechanism assessment.

The paper's subject is crop-trait (LAI, SPAD) retrieval from Sentinel-2 imagery, i.e. agricultural/plant science using machine-learning methodology. It trains a multi-task elastic net (an elastic-net regression variant) on its own field-spectral data in a supervised setting, while MIC feature selection and nested cross-validation are analysis steps rather than model types.

The paper is a multireader multicase clinical evaluation of the commercial qER EU 2.0 tool, which is run as-is on retrospective non-contrast CT head scans with no training, fine-tuning or prompting described, so learning_paradigm is empty. The subject domain is diagnostic head imaging with CT; the tool is tagged verbatim since the abstract gives no architecture, though qER is a well-established deep-learning product.

The paper locally calibrates Esri's pretrained US Solar Panel Detection model on labelled rooftop-solar data via transfer learning (supervised fine-tuning) for solar PV mapping from geospatial imagery, so the pretrained tool is fine-tuned/adapted. The abstract names no underlying architecture, so the model is tagged verbatim, with deep learning and transfer learning as families; no biomedical domain term applies.

The paper trains an ensemble machine-learning prognostic model (supervised) alongside unsupervised single-cell clustering/embedding analyses, and applies existing tools such as cell2location as-is. The specific ensemble algorithms are unnamed (so only the 'ensemble learning' family is tagged), CellChat/Monocle/pySCENIC/inferCNV/PROGENy/stLearn are excluded as bioinformatics pipelines, and cell2location is tagged verbatim with its well-established deep-learning basis.

The paper is a soil/forestry study of medicinal-herb intercropping effects on soil properties and microbial communities characterized by high-throughput (amplicon/metagenomic) sequencing, so its domains are agricultural science and microbiology/microbial ecology. The only ML model named is a random forest trained on the study's data to identify taxa associated with intercropping effects (RDA and LEfSe are excluded statistical analyses).

The paper trains its own lightweight object detector, CFRDet, on a self-built labelled flat-jujube dataset (supervised detection), with the contribution being a deep computer-vision method applied to agricultural fruit detection/harvesting. ASAM, the MIRB heads and Mish activation are architectural components of the detector rather than separate models, so only CFRDet is tagged, with deep learning as its family.

The paper trains a supervised model zoo of logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting on labelled ECG-QRS event samples, plus a cross-subject nearest-neighbour geometry analysis for recoverability estimation. The subject domain is wearable physiological-signal informatics, with the added physical sensor (accelerometry) framing it as a data-acquisition question.

The paper trains its own active-learning models on sparse labelled experimental alloy data (supervised closed-loop design) for physics-based Invar materials discovery, with dataset mining as a secondary theme. No concrete algorithm or architecture is named (only generic 'machine learning analysis' and 'empirical fine-tuning'), so model_type remains empty and active learning is the only attributable model family.

The core subject is a materials-chemistry study of PVDF/BIT piezoelectric composites engineered as flexible wearable sensors for physiological monitoring, with machine learning integrated for classification of motion signals (hence Biomaterials/Bioengineering domains). The abstract names no specific ML algorithm or family, so model_type and model_family stay empty, while supervised training of classifiers on the authors' own sensor data is clearly implied.

The paper trains PLS-based classifiers on ATR-FTIR spectra from IBD biopsy samples (supervised), with PCA and hierarchical clustering as exploratory unsupervised analyses alongside. Domain-wise it targets colorectal cancer risk assessment (oncology) in IBD patients (gastroenterology) as a clinical cohort study.

domain_tier3: ["Protein sites, features and motifs", "Protein interactions", "Molecular modelling"]
rationale: The paper develops a motif-discovery pipeline for LIR/SLiM annotations in virulent-virus proteins, combining sequence pattern matching, IUPred3 disorder prediction, and AlphaFold3 structural modelling, with no model trained or fine-tuned in the study. The subject is virus-host interaction biology (autophagy hijacking by hemorrhagic fever and other virulent viruses), with IUPred3 and AlphaFold3 applied as-is; AlphaFold3 is a well-established deep learning system while no training paradigm applies.

This is a non-biomedical AIOps study on root cause analysis and P95 latency prediction in social media service workflows, best captured by Computer science with Software engineering and Data mining, plus Workflows for the media-consumption workflow subject. A model is fitted on eight weeks of operational data (Top-k accuracy and MAE/RMSE imply supervised learning), but the abstract names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family remain empty.

Four unnamed machine learning feature-selection algorithms were fit on labelled GEO transcriptomic data to rank hub genes, so supervised training applies, but since no algorithm is named the model_type/model_family fields remain empty. The subject is transcriptomic hub-gene discovery in IBD and periodontitis with immune-infiltration and single-cell analyses (Genomics, Immunology, Gene expression, Transcriptomics), plus molecular dynamics screening of candidate COPZ1-binding compounds.

This is an omics-based bioinformatics study building a diagnostic transcriptomic gene signature for lung cancer and VTE, with differential expression, WGCNA and immune-infiltration analyses as pipeline components. The only ML model is LASSO regression trained supervised on public gene-expression data to select the five-gene diagnostic signature.

The study fits MaxEnt species distribution models on occurrence and CMIP6 climate data (with ENMeval for parameter calibration), a supervised presence-background maximum-entropy approach belonging to classical machine learning. The subject domain is plant/crop-wild-relative ecology and conservation in an agricultural breeding context.

domain_tier3: ["Data acquisition", "Data quality management", "Data submission, annotation and curation"]
rationale: This is a corpus-construction resource paper for discourse analysis: a social-media language corpus is acquired, cleaned, quality-checked and annotated with NLP layers (Penn Treebank POS/lemma tagging, semantic fields, discourse-strategy coding). The only AI component is Hermes Agent, an existing agentic AI research assistant executed as-is to run the pipeline, so no model is trained and no learning paradigm applies.

The paper trains its own MCKG-SL model, combining RGCN and GAT graph neural networks with a multi-feature cross-aggregation module on knowledge-graph and multi-omics data, in a supervised synthetic-lethality prediction task. The subject is a computational bioinformatics method for oncogenic KRAS synthetic-lethality prediction, fitting computational biology/bioinformatics with molecular medicine and functional genomics aspects.

A supervised two-stage cascade is trained on layer-/row-wise datasets built by aligning CT-derived pore labels with welding parameters: a logistic regression sentinel and a random forest confirmer (the optional k-of-n smoothing is a non-learned post-processing filter, and EDA is not a model). Subject-wise the work is an ML/AI framework applied to industrial computed tomography data with a data-alignment workflow, mapped to Computer science, Machine learning, Imaging, and Tomography/Data integration.

A clinical oncology study profiling oral/gut microbiota via shotgun metagenomic sequencing to predict neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy response in rectal cancer. The AI prediction model is developed (trained) in this study for supervised classification with an internal test AUC, but since no algorithm, architecture, or named tool is given, model_type and model_family remain empty.

The paper trains a supervised multiple-kernel ridge regression model (three SOAP-derived kernels) on GFN1-xTB band gaps of theoretical COFs to learn interpretable structure-property relationships, placing it in chemistry/computational chemistry with molecular modelling of the COF structures; MKRR is a non-neural kernel method, i.e. classical machine learning, trained from scratch on the study's data (GFN1-xTB and SOAP are chemistry methods/descriptors, not ML models).

The paper trains a Gaussian process classification (Bayesian ML) model on literature-derived composition/elemental descriptors to predict glass-forming ability, i.e. supervised classical machine learning applied to alloy/materials chemistry, validated by sputtered Cu-Zr-Al thin films. No deep learning, LLM, or second learning step is involved.

Five off-the-shelf LLMs (GPT-5.2, Grok, DeepSeek, MedGemma, Claude 4.5 Sonnet) were queried with standardized prompts to produce Angoff estimates, with no weight updates or training, so the models are prompted zero/few-shot and no learning paradigm applies. The subject is AI-assisted standard setting in medical education assessment, best mapped to Medicine with Medical informatics and Machine learning as supporting domains.

A surface-chemistry/catalysis study that develops a machine-learning-accelerated molecular dynamics framework for the Cu-Ag system, implying an ML interatomic potential fitted (trained) on system data, hence supervised learning. The abstract names no specific potential architecture, so no model family is assigned.

A retrospective clinical study that trains ML models (best: XGBoost) on labelled hospital patient data to predict bacterial infection foci, i.e. supervised training of a gradient-boosting ensemble. Venn-ABERS calibration and conformal risk control are calibration/uncertainty techniques, not model types, so they are excluded.

The paper's subject is a flexible MXene/PDMS piezoresistive sensor for physiological and acoustic-vibration sensing, i.e. biomedical device/bioengineering work, with pitch recognition performed by a 1D-CNN trained on the collected sensor signals to 97.5% accuracy (supervised deep learning).

The study is an immunology/vaccination work (B-cell responses to influenza vaccine) with single-cell RNA-seq supporting its findings, so it is tagged Biomedical science, Immunology, Omics, plus Vaccinology, Transcriptomics and Gene expression. Machine learning algorithms were trained on the study's own baseline data to predict seroconversion (supervised), but no specific algorithm or model family is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family are left empty.

The study trains machine-learning interatomic potentials on r2SCAN-level DFT reference data (supervised fitting of energies/forces) and applies them in machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations of aluminosilicate glasses. The subject domain is materials/physical chemistry, with machine learning and molecular dynamics simulation as the central enabling methods; the abstract names no specific architecture, so no model_family beyond the canonical MLIP type is assigned.

The paper trains supervised credit-scoring models on the Home Credit Default Risk dataset and evaluates three named non-neural fairness interventions (AIF360 Reweighing, Fairlearn ExponentiatedGradient and ThresholdOptimizer) as its core methods, so model types are tagged verbatim with the classical machine learning family. The subject is algorithmic fairness in ML credit scoring rather than any biomedical topic, so only the computer science/machine learning domain terms apply.

A supervised risk prediction model for MDR infection was trained on MIMIC-IV data with KNN identified as the optimal algorithm, plus LASSO (with Boruta) for feature selection. The clinical subject is multidrug-resistant infection risk in mechanically ventilated COPD ICU patients, so Medicine/critical care with infectious disease at tier 3.

A retrospective MIMIC-IV cohort study in cardiology that trains supervised ML models for one-year mortality prediction in NSTEMI/STEMI patients; only Random Forest is named among the five algorithms, and it is an ensemble of decision trees, giving classical machine learning plus ensemble learning families.

The paper trains logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting classifiers on the labelled IBM/Kaggle Telco churn dataset and deploys the best one (logistic regression) in a Streamlit dashboard, so it is a supervised study whose own models are trained. The subject is telecom customer analytics rather than biomedicine, so domains are limited to the computer-science/ML tiers.

The paper trains four supervised regression models (XGBoost, random forest, SVM, linear regression) on a curated multi-source dataset of 927 heavy-metal adsorption records to predict biochar adsorption capacity, so ensemble learning and classical ML families apply. SHAP and PDPs are interpretability analyses, not model types, and the subject domain is environmental adsorption chemistry with data integration from multiple sources.

The paper develops and trains LAANet, a deep multimodal fusion network built on a state-space model (Mamba-style SSM) with attention-based modules, for salient object detection on visual-depth-thermal images. Its subject is computer-science/machine-learning methodology applied to image analysis; attention and convolutions are components of the network, so only the SSM architecture is tagged as the model type.

The pipeline trains scaffold-aware ML models (supervised endpoint prediction) while applying existing in-silico toxicity predictors as-is, and PCA is the only named algorithm (docking is a chemistry method, not a model type). No specific ML algorithm for the toxicity predictions is named, so model_type is limited to principal component analysis, giving classical ML plus dimensionality reduction and supervised plus unsupervised paradigms.

The study trains two supervised models on its own data: a Random Forest land-cover classifier and an XGBoost regression for LST variance, both classical-ML ensemble tree methods (SHAP is an explainability method and is excluded). The subject domain is urban environmental/remote-sensing science, which has no matching tier1 term, so tier1 is left empty and tier2 captures Environmental science plus the Machine learning application.

model_type: ["dynamic prompt distribution network (DPDN)", "density-aware multiple instance learning (DA-MIL)"]
rationale: The paper trains its own domain-adaptive open-vocabulary food detection framework, combining a prompt-based network for region-text alignment with weakly supervised image-level MIL, yielding supervised base-category learning plus weak supervision (semi-supervised) and image+text multimodal, transfer/adaptation-based deep learning. Domain tags reflect the computer-vision ML subject applied to food science, with the label filtering/auditing step captured as data quality management.

A non-biomedical financial forecasting study, best captured by the method domains Computer science and Machine learning, with no finance-specific tier3 terms available. The models are trained on the paper's own stock data in a supervised regression setting, and while 'deep learning' is named as the model family, no specific architecture or algorithm (e.g., LSTM, CNN) is given, and feature selection is a task rather than a model type.

The paper trains its own classifiers on labelled burned/unburned Landsat-derived predictors under a supervised chronological design, with a calibrated radial-basis support vector machine as the best-performing model. The subject is forest fire disturbance monitoring in Mediterranean forests, an ecology/environmental-science application within the biology branch; no tier3 term fits the remote-sensing subject well.

The paper trains nine supervised ML models on its own prospective cohort to predict bleeding risk during rivaroxaban therapy, with random forest performing best; LASSO, random forest and XGBoost are the named model types (SMOTEENN is resampling and SHAP is excluded as explainability). The subject is drug-safety/bleeding-risk prediction for an anticoagulant, best captured by Medicine > Pharmacology + Haematology > Pharmacovigilance.

The paper fits an XGBoost model on Vilnius geospatial predictors (NDVI, population density, nighttime lights) to predict PM2.5, so it is supervised training of a gradient-boosting ensemble; SHAP is only an explainability method and LISA a statistical spatial analysis, so neither is a model type. The subject domain is environmental science (urban air quality and grey-green space balance) with machine learning as the methodological domain, and no tier-1 or tier-3 term fits the study's subject.

A clinical proteomics (DIA) study of tuberculosis patients that discovers and validates plasma protein biomarkers, fitting Biomedical science with Biomarkers/Proteomics and the infectious-disease clinical-study context. Four unnamed machine-learning algorithms were trained on labelled STB/MTB data for candidate screening, but since no algorithm is named, model_type and model_family stay empty; Limma and ROC analysis are statistical methods, not models.

The paper fits a sparse PLS-DA model in-house on Cell Painting imaging features to discriminate healthy vs T2D endothelial cell morphology, a supervised classical machine learning approach (PLS-DA maps to the canonical 'partial least squares'). Cell biology/toxicology of an endocrine-disrupting chemical studied by high-content imaging sets the domain, while segmentation and feature extraction are tasks, not model types.

The paper trains four supervised classifiers (ANN, PSO-optimized SVM, Naive Bayes, GA-optimized decision tree) on simulated induction-motor fault data, so model_use is trained-in-study and the paradigm is supervised. The domain is AI/ML fault detection in an engineering simulation setting, best captured by Computer science, Machine learning, Simulation experiment, and Data acquisition; PSO and GA are excluded as model types since they only tune the SVM and decision tree hyperparameters.

The paper develops a regularized Gaussian mixture model fitted by its own MAP-EM procedure (NIW priors, graph-Laplacian, noise component, split-merge) for unsupervised document clustering, so the model is trained in-study with unsupervised learning. The variational Bayesian GMM is only a comparator, and no deep, neural, or language models are involved.

The paper trains an MLP from scratch on ROSMAP scRNA-seq data to classify AD vs control nuclei, and its explicit framing as a 'deep learning framework' places the MLP in the deep learning family; SHAP and the gene regulatory network construction are excluded as explainability/pipeline analyses. The subject is single-cell transcriptomics of microglia in Alzheimer's Disease, so it is tagged as biomedical/neuroscience with transcriptomics and transcription-factor regulation tier-3 terms.

The paper develops a fluorescent nanoparticle nanosensor for small-molecule stress biomarkers (dopamine, noradrenaline, cortisol), with analyte discrimination performed by PLS-DA, a supervised classical ML method built on the study's own fluorescence data. No pretrained, prompted, or deep models are mentioned.

The paper's subject is environmental health risk assessment of fluoride contamination (hazard indices under EPA RAGS vs Korean KRAG guidance), so it is tagged Medicine > Public health and epidemiology + Environmental science > Safety sciences. Explainable machine learning was applied to the study's simulated exposure scenarios, implying a model fitted in-study (supervised), but no algorithm or model family is named, so model_type and model_family remain empty.

DeepSMCA is trained in-house on 914 curated compounds: a VGAE learns PPI network embeddings unsupervised, feeding a supervised ResNetDNN synergy classifier (the Bliss independence model is a pharmacological reference, not an ML model, and unnamed baselines are excluded). The subject is AI-driven anti-aging drug discovery from TCM small molecules, with transcriptomic pathway analysis and preclinical cell validation.

The paper introduces its own neural-network friction models trained supervisedly on a database built from sliding compression tests and finite element simulations, and the abstract names no specific architecture or depth, so the generic 'neural network' with the 'classic neural network' family is used. The subject domain (tribological friction modeling in cold forging) is closest to Physics, with the central finite element simulation work captured by Simulation experiment; explainability analyses and FE simulation are not model types.

The study trains its own semi-supervised framework (explicitly 'semi-supervised cross-lingual financial ontology induction') with a named uncertainty-aware contrastive objective, giving semi-supervised plus self-supervised learning and the representation-learning family. No concrete architecture or algorithm is named (NER, distillation, and attention are a task/technique), so model_type stays empty; the domain is ML/NLP methodology on financial text, not biomedicine.

The paper builds a domain-specific expert system that applies NLP algorithms to turn natural-language requirements into executable code, with no training, fine-tuning, or prompting of any model described, so the system is applied as-is and no learning paradigm applies. The subject is computer science at the NLP/software-engineering intersection, and no tier-3 domain term fits a code-generation system.

The paper develops a logistic prediction model on its own retrospective insulinoma cohort (with AUC/ROC evaluation and risk stratification), i.e. supervised classical ML trained in this study. The subject is clinical prediction of metastasis in a rare endocrine tumor, so the domains centre on medicine, endocrinology/oncology and clinical studies of a rare disease.

stPainter is the paper's own conditional latent diffusion generative model, pretrained in this study on a pan-cancer scRNA-seq atlas via a denoising objective (self-supervised) and then applied to new spatial transcriptomics datasets without retraining. Its subject domain is enhancing and analyzing spatial transcriptomics/gene-expression data for tumor microenvironment studies.

Supervised regression models are trained on the authors' own small experimental datasets to predict Coulombic efficiency, guided by physics-derived 3D solvation-structure descriptors (Li^SSL) and interpreted via explainable ML. No specific algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_type is empty, while the physics-guided descriptor framework makes physics-informed machine learning the appropriate family; the subject domain is battery electrolyte chemistry.

The paper trains a non-deep ML pipeline on its own eggshell-image data, engineering physically motivated wavelet-transform features (explicitly instead of deep learning) that feed an unnamed supervised regression predicting the colour trait. The subject is livestock-breeding phenotyping, so domain terms capture agriculture, phenomics and the genotype-phenotype link; only the wavelet transform is a named algorithm, and no specific learner is given beyond generic 'machine learning'.

The paper trains its own hybrid forecasting model on historical outbreak data for crown-of-thorns starfish, clearly implying supervised learning, but it names no specific ML algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family stay empty (the mechanistic larval-dispersal component is a process/simulation model, not an ML model type). The subject domain is ecology of a marine species on the Great Barrier Reef.

The paper's subject is population-level epidemiology of physical inactivity and NCD burden (Medicine -> Public health and epidemiology). XGBoost is trained on the panel data for supervised projection of NCD burden; the fixed-effects regression and PLS-SEM are association/mediation analyses rather than predictive models, and SHAP and multiple imputation are excluded as explainability/preprocessing methods.

The authors generated >38 million temporal protein-abundance measurements and developed/pretrained ProteinTalks on this in-house perturbation proteomics resource, learning transferable dynamical latent representations from proteome trajectories (self-supervised pretraining) before applying it to supervised drug-discovery predictions (efficacy, synergy, patient response stratification). The subject is a computational virtual-cell model for in silico drug discovery built on proteomics, extended to patient organoids and clinical biopsies; the abstract names no specific architecture, so the model is tagged verbatim as ProteinTalks.

A prospective multi-centre clinical evaluation in oncology of an in-house guideline-based decision-support pipeline, so the domain is Medicine/Oncology with Medical informatics and clinical studies. No training or fine-tuning is described: the pipeline ingests, structures and normalizes patient data and guidelines and applies an existing LLM (behind a rule-based 80% supervisory threshold) for decision-making, hence no learning paradigm.

The paper mechanistically characterizes the M. tuberculosis enzyme PimA as an anti-tubercular drug target, using the pretrained AlphaFold2 model for structure prediction (no model is trained in the study; docking and mutagenesis are not ML model types). AlphaFold2 is established as a deep learning model applied as-is.

A cross-sectional clinical epidemiology study of sarcopenia risk in diabetic adults, fitting causal forest (random-forest-based) algorithms to NHANES-style data to estimate heterogeneous conditional associations; the linear/logistic regressions and cubic splines are association-testing statistics, not predictive models, so only the causal forest is tagged as a trained supervised model.

A surface-chemistry paper on hydrogen tunneling in a CHCH2 species on Cu(110), studied experimentally by single-molecule STM and corroborated by deep-learning-assisted path-integral Monte Carlo simulations of the system, so the deep-learning model is trained on the paper's own data (supervised fitting). No specific architecture or named ML model is given, so model_type is left empty, with 'deep learning' as the only family, and the chemistry domains (computational chemistry for the simulations, analytical chemistry for STM characterization, molecular modelling and small molecules at tier 3) capture the subject matter.

The paper trains XGBoost, random forest, LASSO and SVM-RFE on its own GEO/TCGA transcriptomic data to converge on NSCLC key genes, i.e. supervised classical/ensemble ML; WGCNA, CIBERSORTx, Mendelian randomization, ceRNA/TF networks, CMap and docking are pipelines, statistical analyses or simulation methods, not tagged models. The domain is oncology-focused bioinformatics over bulk transcriptomic profiles with genotype-phenotype causal inference (MR) and experimental validation.

The paper's subject is immune-microbiota mechanisms in endometriosis, studied via single-cell/bulk transcriptomics (DEGs, hub genes), gut microbiome-metabolite analysis, and molecular simulations of metabolite-target binding. The only ML evidence is SHAP, an explainability method implying an unnamed supervised predictive model fit on the study's data, so no model type or family can be tagged from the abstract.

The pretrained oncoPredict tool (a ridge-regression-based classical ML method) is applied as-is to predict CDK4/6 inhibitor sensitivity from TCGA/GDSC2 data, while a separate unnamed machine-learning step trained on the study's own data selects core lncRNAs, implying supervised learning. Domains reflect an oncology biomarker study centred on transcriptomic drug-sensitivity pharmacogenomics.

The paper trains a simulator-in-the-loop learner in which a hybrid evolutionary-strategy / soft actor-critic controller is guided by a critic converting simulator feedback into action-value signals (soft actor-critic normalized to the canonical 'policy gradient'), while accepted trajectories are recycled as confidence-weighted pseudo-labels, giving reinforcement plus semi-supervised learning; the evolutionary strategy is a classical non-neural method and the structural prior's architecture is unnamed, so no family is guessed for it. The domain is protein sequence-environment learning with CASP14 contact prediction, driven by an all-atom molecular-dynamics simulator, which is excluded from model_type as a simulation method.

The paper is a metabolomics/compound-annotation study whose contribution is an LLM-driven multiagent system that orchestrates existing annotation tools (SIRIUS, FLARE, JESTR, DiffMS) through a natural-language interface, with no model training or fine-tuning reported. Hence the LLM is prompted and no learning paradigm applies, while the domain spans metabolomics, chemical structure identification, and multitool workflow integration.

A food-microbiology study that experimentally measured Salmonella thermal inactivation in ready-to-use therapeutic food and trained neural network models on those time-temperature inactivation data (supervised regression, validated with RMSE/R2) to predict pathogen die-off. The abstract names only plain 'neural network (NN)' models with no deep architecture, so the family is classic neural network; the unnamed 'conventional models' of the title are not tagged as no algorithm is specified.

A cognitive-neuroscience fMRI study (spatiotemporal and intersubject RSA) of trait impression updating, so Biology > Neurobiology with Imaging/MRI for the functional neuroimaging. Pre-trained ML models annotated facial, vocal and speech features and deep neural networks performed compression, multimodal fusion, temporal integration and prediction, all applied without any training reported, yielding no learning paradigm and only the explicitly named deep 'neural network' type.

The paper trains multimodal fusion models on MIMIC-CXR image-report pairs for supervised multi-label classification of thoracic pathologies, comparing encoder combinations (ViT, ClinicalBERT) and proposing a GMU-based gated fusion architecture. ViT and BERT/ClinicalBERT are named deep models (BERT mapping to the LLM family), and the joint image+text gating makes multimodal learning a defining family of the work.

Regularized XGBoost regressors and classifiers were trained in-study on supervised targets (condensate affinity/partitioning) using RDKit physicochemical descriptors, so the models are classical-ML ensemble members; RDKit is a descriptor toolkit and SHAP an explainability method, neither of which is a model type. The subject spans cheminformatics (logD/logP/logS ionization-dependent partitioning) applied to cell-biological phase separation of small molecules.

A FAERS pharmacovigilance study fitting disproportionality models (reporting odds ratio plus the shallow Bayesian confidence propagation neural network) and LASSO feature refinement on its own data, followed by machine-learning-based candidate-gene prioritization on integrated OA transcriptomic data. Domains center on drug-safety/musculoskeletal medicine with transcriptomics-level gene prioritization; only the two named algorithms are tagged as model types.

The paper develops a data-driven battery-electrolyte interphase framework that integrates DFT with machine-learning interatomic potentials (trained on the study's DFT data, i.e. supervised regression) and applies unsupervised clustering to screen electrolyte additives, giving a second unsupervised learning step; descriptor-based computational screening of small-molecule additives supports the computational chemistry/cheminformatics tagging. The MLIP is tagged verbatim as its own model type (the canonical list assigns it no family), while the clustering falls under classical machine learning; DFT and distribution-of-relaxation-time analysis are excluded as non-ML chemistry/analysis methods.

The paper trains its own machine-learning classification and QSAR models (supervised, classical statistical learning) to screen a large compound library for TRPV1 antagonists, so 'trained in this study' and 'supervised' apply. No specific ML algorithm is named beyond QSAR; the 3D shape-similarity screening and molecular dynamics simulations are non-ML chemistry methods and are excluded from model_type.

The paper applies an existing multilingual machine learning model to rate goal orientations in political texts, with no training or fine-tuning described, so it is 'pretrained, applied as-is' and nothing is learned in-paper; no algorithm, architecture, or named tool is given, so model_type is empty and only the NLP family is evidenced by the multilingual text-rating task. The subject is environmental (climate-policy support) communication analysed with text rating, with no tier-1 or tier-3 term genuinely applicable.

rationale: HS-MIND is a multi-agent clinical decision-support system built on a reasoning-augmented LLM that is used at inference time via RAG, controlled chain-of-thought and tool-augmented reasoning, with no training or fine-tuning of models reported. The subject is medical-informatics decision support for digestive malignancies, evaluated in a single-centre series of 25 older patients.

RankReg, a ranking-regression model with a hybrid loss, is trained on experimentally measured fitness values and used to guide successive rounds of model-directed variant selection in a closed loop, i.e. supervised active learning; its underlying architecture is not specified, so only the named model is tagged. The subject is AI-driven enzyme (protein) engineering demonstrated on P450 BM3 and Sortase A, giving Biotechnology/Proteins with Enzymes, Protein variants and Protein properties.

rationale: The subject is geotechnical strength prediction, which has no match in the biomedical EDAM tiers, so only the methodological domain 'Machine learning' is tagged. Six supervised regressors (MLR, SVR, RF, XGBoost, CatBoost, BP-ANN) are trained on the study's own 180-specimen data, giving families classical ML, ensemble learning, and a shallow (non-deep) classic neural network; PSO is only hyperparameter tuning and SHAP/Monte Carlo UQ are excluded per the model-type rules.

The study trains random forest and XGBoost on simulated and UK Biobank individual-level data to predict genetic risk, benchmarking them against the standard additive polygenic risk score, so the models are supervised and span classical/ensemble learning. The subject domain is genome-wide genetic architecture and disease prediction, centering on quantitative genetics and nonadditive (epistatic) interaction variance in humans.

A single-nucleus RNA-seq and ATAC-seq study of macaque spermatogenesis across developmental stages, i.e. developmental biology investigated through transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility (epigenomic) profiling. The only ML component is unsupervised clustering applied to the integrated single-cell dataset (no algorithm named, so tagged generically), while differential expression, GO/motif enrichment and pseudotime trajectory analysis are excluded bioinformatics analyses.

ProRB is a sequence-based multi-task deep learning framework trained in this study for binding-affinity and interface prediction plus RNA sequence generation, while pretrained protein and RNA language models are applied as-is to supply embeddings; training on labelled interaction data is supervised, and the generative component motivates the generative-AI family. The subject domains centre on computational analysis of protein-RNA interactions, spanning proteins and nucleic acids with protein-interaction, RNA, and regulatory/functional RNA specifics.

FEDRA fits an unsupervised clustering step on transformer-based semantic embeddings (pretrained, applied as-is) with graph-based co-occurrence and frequency/network ranking to extract decision factors from text, and validates the rankings against an LLM-based benchmark used via prompting. The subject is a general text-mining/NLP methodology for decision-support knowledge extraction (case study on wastewater plant siting), not a biomedical application.
